units.en: Spam these decisions for the rest of the game to make your Navy steadily stronger over time.
In December 1939, begin to justify a War goal on ⟦0⟧. It should take you roughly 100 days and be done in early April 1939, which is right when the Winter War should be ending.
Plan a pair of Naval invasions from Memel to Helsinki and from Memel to Turku.
Split your fleet into roughly 3 equal parts and Patrol in the Lower Baltic Sea, the Gulf of Bothnia, and the Gulf of Finland.
When the ⟦0⟧ peace out with ⟦1⟧, taking Karelia, declare war and launch your naval invasions.

From here, bring over the rest of your forces and slowly defeat the Finnish. You can micro against them to create surrounds and take easy ⟦0⟧ or you can just battle plan all the way north; it really doesn't matter very much. You effectively have infinite manpower because of your advisor, so the only thing you're losing equipment, which is just time.
Annex them and take their navy as well.

From here, the goal is to strike the ⟦0⟧ in mid-1942 with 48-60 divisions at a time when your technology is finally back up to par. However, you can't afford to wait any longer than mid-1942 because the ⟦1⟧ AI is busy committing suicide, and they are highly skilled at doing this.
Research Landing Ships. You will soon need the ability to plan 4 naval invasions at once.

Make sure you're continuing your Collaboration Governments on the ⟦0⟧ and doing your "Refit ships to Cruisers" decision every time you can. (The destroyers one is nice but ultimately less impactful.) If your number of convoys begins to drop over time, build 2-3 Naval dockyards. It should start going back up after that.
If your number of convoys begins to drop over time, build 2-3 ⟦0⟧. It should start going back up after that.

Good uses of ⟦0⟧: Switch out the Nazi Sympathizer for the Prince of Terror and the Progressive Doctor for the Compassionate Gentleman. This will help keep your Compliance up and your Resistance down. Fill out your Military Staff where possible - grab the Artillery (Specialist) and Army Logistics (Expert). Save the third slot for your first General to reach level 4, who you'll want promote to Infantry (Specialist) and hire immediately. After you get your initial round of Military factories built in all of your states, you'll also want to drop Free Trade down to Limited Exports. Grab the Siemens Iceland Industrial Concern when you can; it's a decent research boost and reduces the amount of Coal required as well.
Switch out the ⟦0⟧ for the ⟦1⟧ and the ⟦2⟧ for the ⟦3⟧. This will help keep your Compliance up and your Resistance down.
Fill out your Military Staff where possible - grab the ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧. Save the third slot for your first General to reach level 4, who you'll want promote to ⟦2⟧ and hire immediately.
After you get your initial round of ⟦0⟧ built in all of your states, you'll also want to drop ⟦1⟧ down to ⟦2⟧.
Grab the Siemens Iceland Industrial Concern when you can; it's a decent research boost and reduces the amount of ⟦0⟧ required as well.
By early 1942, get all your troops lined up and trained on the coast of the Netherlands and begin setting up your naval invasions. Personally, I prefer the following four invasions:
From Rotterdam to the tile between Portsmouth and Dover.
From Rotterdam to the tile south of London, the tile east of London, and the tile south of Ipswich.
From Leeuwarden to Hull and the tile north of Hull.
From Leeuwarden to the tile north of Newcastle, Newcastle, and the tile south of Newcastle.
The first two naval invasions go through the English Channel, and the second two naval invasions go through the Eastern North Sea and the North Sea.
The moment you make these naval invasion plans, the AI becomes aware of them and attempts to defend against them by bolstering their Naval Dominance in the English Channel and the North Sea.

However, because you made plans that are split between 2 regions and because your fleet can provide upwards of 2000 Naval Dominance in a single region, the ⟦0⟧ AI physically cannot get enough Naval Dominance to block all 4 naval invasions simultaneously. By the way, I recommend pulling your submarines off the main fleet into a second one and setting that second fleet to patrol only in the Eastern North Sea. All ~25 submarines you have should give you just over 150 Naval Dominance, and the UK does not contest the Eastern North Sea against you until after the war starts.

All ~25 submarines you have should give you just over 150 Naval Dominance, and the ⟦0⟧ does not contest the Eastern North Sea against you until after the war starts.

At this point, pick one of the two sets of naval invasions to commit to. Assign divisions to that set of naval invasions and put your main fleet on Patrol in the needed sea area. This trick exploits that when a war starts, the Naval dominance values established before a war starts are retained. If you just threw your fleet in these sea zones while already at war with the UK, they would have immediately engaged and wrecked your fleet before you were able to reach the Naval dominance threshold required for your invasions.

If you just threw your fleet in these sea zones while already at war with the UK, they would have immediately engaged and wrecked your fleet before you were able to reach the Naval dominance threshold required for your invasions.
When one set of the naval invasions lists as "ready", go ahead and finally War goal justification on the UK and then declare war, launching the invasions immediately.
Quickly, switch your fleet over to Naval Invasion Support. Watch the landing carefully.
Out of the gate, we've chosen to avoid landing directly on ports for the most part in order to avoid the steep penalties associated with naval attacks against ⟦0⟧.

But that means the second you land, you need to Force Attack with most of your divisions on the adjacent ports, while using your other couple of divisions to immediately walk around the port. If you manage to walk around it fully, isolating it, then you will usually instantly win the fight due to the encirclement penalty.

As soon as you've got a port, set up a Field Marshal frontline and assign all of your forces to it (minus like 4 divisions left at home to guard Iceland). Also, set all your ships on Hold now so they return to port. You don't want them fighting the Royal Navy if you can help it.
Also, set all your ships on Hold now so they return to port. You don't want them fighting the Royal Navy if you can help it.

At this point, I recommend throwing up a quick offensive line at the opposite end of the Home Islands from where you landed and setting your battle plans to Aggressive (at least at first). That combined with some manual micro, especially at the start, can help you get some good surrounds and capture some key ports.

However, this is by far the hardest part of the run. You will likely eventually enter a stalemate against the ⟦0⟧ when you control about half of the country, and this stalemale can often be incredibly hard to break.
It can be worth it to stop pushing entirely in order to allow your units time to resupply and refill their organization.

However, remember that you have a +40% Division attack bonus for your units (possibly the single strongest division attack bonus in the entire game) through National Spirits but only a +15% Division defense bonus. This means you can sometimes get into situations where you can't hold ground against the ⟦0⟧ forces but you can still push them.
If you just got the achievement upon capitulating the ⟦0⟧, congratulations! You're free from this achievement and can stop reading here.

If you didn't get it, don't worry too much. Due to the way the game combines similar wars between factions, sometimes your "Iceland-UK" war is automatically combined into the much larger "Germany-Poland" war. This depends on a few different factors that you can't control, including who the AI actually decides to call in to each war and whether or not the "Italy-Ethiopia" war was already combined with the "Germany-Poland" war. If your war was folded into the larger war, then you may not have had the required war participation to be "the country who was primarily responsible for capitulating the UK" and thus not earned the achievement. Is this fixable? Yes. Will it be fast? Probably not. What needs to happen now is you need to capitulate the remaining major powers in the Allies (the USA and possibly Brazil and/or Argentina), act a certain way in the peace deal (keep their land from being puppeted so their tag is unused), and then release the UK again as an independent sovereign nation (which prioritizes using the original UK tag again if it is currently unused). Then, you just declare war on them again (alone) and run them over in a couple days. This will count, and you'll actually get the achievement.

Is this fixable? Yes. Will it be fast? Probably not.

What needs to happen now is you need to capitulate the remaining major powers in the ⟦0⟧ (the ⟦1⟧ and possibly ⟦2⟧ and/or ⟦3⟧), act a certain way in the peace deal (keep their land from being puppeted so their tag is unused), and then release the ⟦4⟧ again as an independent sovereign nation (which prioritizes using the original ⟦5⟧ tag again if it is currently unused). Then, you just declare war on them again (alone) and run them over in a couple days. This will count, and you'll actually get the achievement.

You'll need to immediately turn your attention towards mainland Europe. Join all wars that the ⟦0⟧ is in (if you aren't already) and retake France, Italy, and the Balkans. Afterwards, you'll need to capitulate the ⟦1⟧. All the while, you will have to leave a beefy naval garrison in place on the Home Islands (at minimum one full army) because the ⟦2⟧ will constantly naval invade it.

However, this shouldn't be too hard. Because of the Collaboration Governments on the ⟦0⟧, you will now have nearly 300 factories, including nearly 60 dockyards. You can start churning out an actually respectable navy while cleaning up the ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ ones. Once their navies are crippled, you can cut the supplies going to their European fronts, starving their European armies.

It will probably take you a while to build up your army and navy (and heck, if you've got the time, might as well pump out an airforce too; it helps in ⟦0⟧), but none of this should be particularly difficult compared to that fight against the ⟦1⟧.

When you do eventually get a peace deal, annex all of the ⟦0⟧ directly. If the AI is fighting you over a piece of land, you can let them have it, as long as they are choosing to "Take State" and not create a puppet, liberate, or change government.

Afterwards, release all of the puppets possible from the ⟦0⟧'s land that are -not- the ⟦1⟧ ( ⟦2⟧, Wales, ⟦3⟧, and all the various overseas ones). Then release the ⟦4⟧ but as an independent country, not a puppet. If everything went right, the UK you just released should have the normal British focus tree. If it doesn't, somebody probably puppeted some land from them and you didn't notice.
If everything went right, the ⟦0⟧ you just released should have the normal ⟦1⟧ focus tree. If it doesn't, somebody probably puppeted some land from them and you didn't notice.
Justify a War goal on them, line up all your troops on the border in ⟦0⟧ and Wales. Once the justification finishes, declare war, call in your puppets (to use their land to attack), and crush them.
…and you get a canton, everybody gets a canton!
